# /start

Set yourself up in Claude Code properly, in one command.

Most people install Claude Code, type a prompt, get a decent answer, and stop. Nothing
compounds, because nothing gets written down. `/start` fixes that in a single pass.

## What it does

1. **Interviews you.** Six questions about how you actually work, one at a time.
2. **Writes your global `CLAUDE.md`** from your answers, in your words, under 200 lines.
3. **Makes one project folder** for the job that matters most, with its own short brief.
4. **Turns memory on**, so you stop re-explaining yourself.
5. **Audits what you actually do.** It reads your own prompt history and finds the phrases you
   retype and the corrections you keep giving. Those are your first skill and your first hook,
   and it builds them. No history yet? It builds them from your interview answers instead.
6. **Installs the three plugins worth having on day one.** Borrowing beats building.
7. **Shows you auto mode**, the one setting that stops the approve-this-approve-that loop.
8. **Gives you a handover prompt** for when a session gets long.
9. **Sets up one routine**, so something runs without you at the keyboard.
10. **Connects one tool** you already live in.

One of each. Not six folders, not twelve plugins, not a skill library you will never open.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/charlie947/start.git
cp -r start/skills/start ~/.claude/skills/
```

Then in Claude Code:

```
/start
```

## Why it is shaped like this

I ran Claude Code every day for 173 days before writing this. The three things I would do
differently are all the same mistake: **I added faster than I checked.** I built skills I never
used, wrote instructions one bad session at a time, and installed my first plugins on day 36
when they should have gone in during week one.

So this gives you one of everything that compounds, built from evidence about how you actually
work rather than how I do, and nothing you have not earned.

Charlie Hills · [charliehills.substack.com](https://charliehills.substack.com)
